name: Gagauz
catalog_quote: Ударение. В гагаузских словах ударение падает преимущественно на последний слог, т.к. в большинстве своем аффиксы являются ударными, напр.: açík 'открытый', okumáa 'читать', kızkardáş 'сестра' и др. Если последний аффикс в слове неударный, то ударение падает на предшествующий слог, напр.: gagaúzça 'по-гагаузски', insánım 'я - человек', yapárdı 'он делал' и др. audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Coding: fixed final stress (final stress), word domain. Three primary statements agree and are now all held by the project: Pokrovskaja 1973 p.621 (downloaded now, verbatim match to the record's 'sources' text incl. page marker), Pokrovskaja 1997 Jazyki mira p.227 §2.1.2 (held scanned: 'Ударение … падает преимущественно на последний слог'), and Soroceanu pp.6-7 (held PDF, the domain quotation verbatim). StressTyp2 ('final, all word sizes') and Gordon 2002 ('Final') concur. The deciding author is the language's principal grammarian, so the source is authoritative even though the held items are sketch-length; hence 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced' — the full 1964 Nauka grammar (the real best source, and the one StressTyp2 cites) is not yet obtained and no open copy exists. Web checks (CrossRef, Semantic Scholar, Knowledge Commons, archive.org, Kramerius, altaica.ru

sources.quote: "STRESS. In Gagauz words stress falls predominantly on the last syllable, since the majority of affixes are stressed, e.g. al-dy-lar '(they) took', oku-maa 'to read', kalabalyk 'crowd', ikindzhi 'second'. If the last affix in a word is unstressed, stress falls on the preceding syllable (affixal or root), e.g. yazma 'don't write', gagauzcha 'in Gagauz', balykchyyym 'I am a fisherman', giderdi '(he) used to go'.
